reason: Both identify the same root cause at the same location: the subquery filters on status = 'failed' instead of status != 'failed', so it selects the newest failed run rather than the newest non-failed one. Both also describe the same two downstream consequences: (1) when there's nothing to join to that failed-run selection (ground truth: no run has ever failed → NULL; reviewer: failed run has no category rows → clears), the gauge goes empty/silent; (2) when a failed run does have data, that unobserved/bad state gets shown instead of the last real observation (ground truth: overwrites last real observation; reviewer: displays backlog recorded by a failed run). This is a paraphrase of the same mechanism and runtime misbehavior, not a different bug or vague complaint.
